facts.label: legend
facts.quote: It is also believed that Chhath was started by Karna, the son of Surya who ruled over the Anga Desh during the Mahabharat Age.
facts.text: Regional folklore in Bihar asserts that Karna, ruling from Anga, initiated the ritual of standing waist-deep in river water to offer Arghya to Surya, thereby inspiring the core observance of Chhath Puja.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Excavation was taken up in three areas: CMP-1M, CMP-2A and CMP-2B, with a view to exposing the pre-Northern Black Polished Ware levels.
facts.text: Excavations at Champanagar near modern Bhagalpur, identified with the ancient Anga capital Champa, carried out by Patna University and the Archaeological Survey of India, exposed occupational levels beginning before 1000 BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Ancient Champa, capital of Anga, was surrounded by fortifications and a moat.
facts.text: Archaeological excavations at Champanagar revealed an early historic mud rampart, a defensive brick wall, and a surrounding moat encircling the ancient city.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The stories that Sita kept Chhath at Munger, or that Karna founded it in Anga, are local traditions layered onto an older folk observance.
facts.source_name: Chhath: Historical Analysis and Folk Traditions
facts.text: While regional folklore across Bihar attributes the origin of Chhath Puja to Karna's penance in Anga, historians point out that ancient Sanskrit texts contain no reference to Karna founding the festival, arguing instead that Chhath originated as an ancient folk and Vedic solar celebration.
